transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to take up too much of your time if someone else needs it more. But I guess what finally brought me in is... well, things have just felt a little flat lately? 

I mean, I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do! I'm a social worker, so I know how important it is to keep up with my obligations, and I'm definitely still doing that. It's just... I feel like the part of me that used to really reach out to people, or, you know, take pleasure in my work, or my yoga classes, going to art galleries, even just my journaling... it’s all just gone very quiet. I’m mostly just moving through the motions right now. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I wouldn't use the word depressed, really. I'm certainly not crying or feeling deeply sad most of the day. I know how heavy that can be for people, especially from what I see in my work, and I definitely wouldn't want to claim I'm dealing with that when I'm not. 

It's more just... a lack of feeling, rather than a bad feeling? I'm sorry, I hope I'm making sense. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that helpful at all?
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

Um... well, I guess it kind of goes back to what I was mentioning a moment ago, about my yoga and my journaling? I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest, because I do still go, and I still make time for them! I really don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around or giving up on things, because I'm definitely still participating. 

It's just... maybe the joy or the reward from doing them isn't quite as sharp as it used to be. But I'm still trying my very best to stay engaged with it all. I hope that answers your question properly? I know you probably need a more straightforward answer for your notes, I'm sorry if I'm overcomplicating it.
Has this low mood or lack of interest been going on most days for at least two years?

Oh, goodness, no. Definitely not two years. I really hope I didn't make it sound like it's been going on that long! I... well, I like to think I'm usually quite proactive about my well-being, especially given my field. 

It's really just been more of a recent shift. Just the last little while that things have felt so... quiet. I definitely wouldn't have let it go on for years without trying to address it, I promise. Does that help clarify things? I just really don't want to give you the wrong impression and make it seem like I've been neglecting myself for years.
Have these symptoms made it difficult for you to keep up with work, home responsibilities, or relationships?

Oh... well, I want to be completely honest with you, but I also don't want to sound like I'm failing. I am definitely still showing up to work every day! I make sure of that, I'd never just abandon my responsibilities. 

But... I suppose it has been a little bit difficult lately. I'm so embarrassed to admit this, especially being a social worker myself, but I've actually missed a couple of grant deadlines recently. And... my supervisor is wonderful, she really is, but I think she's noticed I'm not quite functioning at my usual level right now. She's quietly moved a few of my more demanding clients over to other clinicians. 

I'm very grateful for her help, of course, but it's hard not to feel like I'm letting the agency down. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent... I am still handling the rest of my caseload just fine, I promise! Does that give you what you need for your assessment? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Have you had any thoughts or experiences that other people would think are not real?

Oh... um. Well. That’s a... that's a very thorough question. I know exactly what you're asking, given my background, and I... I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything like that! I'm still very grounded, I promise. 

It's just... well, I know it probably sounds highly unlikely to anyone else, but... I've become convinced recently that certain comments in our general staff emails, and even just the specific way people pause when they walk past my office door... I feel like they're meant to signal that I'm being watched? Or secretly evaluated. My supervisor has been very sweet and tried to reassure me that it isn't happening, but... I just haven't really been able to shake that feeling, no matter how hard I try to rationalize it.

I know exactly how it sounds, and I'm really trying my absolute best to look at it logically. I hope sharing that doesn't make me sound completely unreasonable? I just want to make sure I'm answering you honestly so you have exactly what you need for your evaluation. Is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people couldn’t?

Oh, no, no. Nothing like that. I... I really want to be clear about that, because I know how important it is to distinguish between, you know, being overly suspicious and actually experiencing hallucinations. 

I've never heard voices or seen things that aren't there. My senses are completely intact, I promise! It's really just that... that feeling of being watched or evaluated that I mentioned. But no actual voices or visions or anything of that sort. I hope that helps reassure you that I'm still very much tethered to reality in that way! Does that answer your question clearly enough? I just want to be absolutely sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had any thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

Oh, my goodness, no. No, absolutely not. I... I would never do anything like that. 

I know it's standard procedure to ask, and I'm so glad you're being thorough—it's so important to check on these things! But I really want to assure you that I haven't had any thoughts of harming myself or... or anything like that. Even with the stress at work and... and those uncomfortable feelings I mentioned, I still value my life very much. I have a lot to live for, and I would never want to cause that kind of pain to anyone around me.

I'm doing my best to cope with everything, I really am. I hope my answers today haven't made you worry about my safety in that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a complete picture, but also reassuring you that I'm completely safe. Is that helpful for your notes?
Have you mostly been able to continue working and taking care of your daily responsibilities, or have you had to stop them because of how you’ve been feeling?

Oh, yes, definitely. I am absolutely still showing up to work every day! I know how critical continuity of care is in our field, so I would never just abandon my responsibilities. I’m doing my very best to keep everything running as smoothly as possible. 

Though... um... I suppose if I'm being completely transparent for your evaluation... things have been just a little bit of a struggle lately. It's nothing catastrophic, I promise! But I did, unfortunately, miss a couple of grant deadlines recently, which is terribly embarrassing and so unlike me. And my supervisor—who is just incredibly supportive—she’s quietly moved a few of my more demanding clients over to other clinicians for the time being. 

I think she just noticed I’m not quite functioning at my usual level right now, with the stress and the... the emails and everything. But I'm still there, and I'm still working hard with the clients I have! I really hope that doesn't make me sound incapable or anything? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest picture you need. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for?
During this period, have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people don’t?

Oh, um... no. Like I... I think I mentioned a little earlier, I really haven't had anything like that happen. I know sometimes in these assessments you have to circle back to certain questions just to be absolutely thorough, which I completely understand! It's so important to double-check these things. 

But yes, my answer is still no to any voices or... or seeing things that aren't there. My perception is still very clear on that front, I promise. I hope it's okay that I'm just repeating my earlier answer? I really want to make sure I'm being as helpful and consistent as possible for your evaluation. Are we still on the right track here?
Have you had any beliefs or experiences like feeling watched or evaluated that you knew were probably not real?

Well... um... I know it sounds a little silly, and I’m honestly a bit embarrassed to admit this, especially given my professional background... but, yes, I suppose I have been dealing with something along those lines. 

I know it sounds incredibly unlikely, but... I’ve become convinced that certain comments in the staff emails, and... and even just the way people pause outside my office door, are meant to signal that I’m being watched or evaluated. 

My supervisor—who is just so wonderful and patient, as I mentioned—has tried to reassure me that nobody is scrutinizing me like that. But for some reason, her reassurance just hasn’t really shaken that feeling for me. I know logically it might not be real, but it just feels so palpable. I really hope sharing that doesn't make me seem completely unreasonable or... or incapable? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions honestly and giving you what you need. Is that the kind of experience you were asking about?
Have you noticed any voices or messages that seem to tell you negative things about yourself, your work, or what might happen to you?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I know we touched on the topic of voices just a moment ago, and I really want to be as helpful and thorough as possible for you, but I truly haven't experienced anything like that. No voices or... or messages telling me bad things about myself or my work. 

I know I mentioned feeling a bit scrutinized by the staff emails earlier, but they don't actually *say* negative things to me, if that makes sense? It's really just that... that underlying feeling of being watched, not any actual voices putting me down or threatening my job. 

I hope I'm making sense? I just really want to ensure I'm not giving you the wrong impression and that I'm giving you the exact information you need. Is that helpful for your notes?
Do you believe the staff emails and people outside your office are definitely sending you secret messages about being watched, even when there’s clear evidence to the contrary?

Well... um... I know it sounds so strange, especially for someone in my field. I really try to look at things objectively, I do. But... yes, I suppose I do still feel that way, even when my supervisor shows me there's no proof. 

Like, she'll go through the emails with me and explain exactly what the staff meant, and logically, I hear her. But... the feeling just doesn't go away. I still just feel so convinced that those little comments, or... or when someone stops outside my door for just a second too long... that they are definitely signals. It's like I can't shake the feeling that I'm being evaluated, no matter how much evidence there is to the contrary. 

I'm really sorry if that makes me sound difficult or... or like I'm not trying hard enough to be rational. I am trying, I promise. I just want to be completely transparent with you so you have everything you need. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly.
Have you been unable to do your work or daily activities most days because of how you’ve been feeling?

Well... um... I wouldn't say I've been *unable* to do my work. I'm definitely still showing up every day, and I'm really trying my best to keep everything on track. I know how important my role is, and I don't want to let anyone down. 

But... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture—I haven't been functioning at my usual level. I... I did miss a couple of grant deadlines recently, which is so unlike me, and I felt terrible about it. And my supervisor, who is just incredibly supportive, has quietly moved a few of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. She framed it as just balancing the caseload, but... I know it's because I've been struggling a bit with everything going on. 

I'm still managing my day-to-day activities, though! I just... I might be a little slower right now. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm failing at my job. I really am trying to push through it. Is that the kind of detail you needed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have other people noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?

Oh, no, I don't think so. Um... I haven't had anyone say anything to me about moving slowly or talking differently. I really try to stay upbeat and keep my energy up at work, especially around the clients and the rest of the team. 

I mean, maybe I've been a little quieter than usual in meetings lately, just because I'm trying to be careful and... and process things. But no one has mentioned me being sluggish or anything like that. I always try to present myself professionally. 

I hope that's okay? I just really haven't noticed anyone looking at me strangely for how I'm moving or talking. Does that answer your question alright?
Have you been having any problems with your sleep lately?

Well, um... no, I don't think my sleep has been a problem. I've been getting my rest. I mean, maybe it takes me just a little longer to wind down at night with... with everything on my mind, but I'm definitely still sleeping. 

I make sure to keep a good routine because I know how important sleep is for my work. I really try to take care of myself that way so I can be present for my clients. I wouldn't say I'm having any real problems with it. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you also been feeling unusually tired or having very little energy most days?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I've been unusually tired. I mean, I definitely feel a normal amount of fatigue by Friday afternoon, but I think that's just part of being in my field, you know? It's emotionally demanding work, and I put a lot of my heart into it. 

But I always make sure I have enough energy to get up and do what needs to be done. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm slacking or not pulling my weight. So, no, I definitely don't feel like I have very little energy most days. I really try to stay active and engaged, and keep a good attitude about everything. 

Is... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you exactly what you need to know.
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have become noticeably slower than usual?

Um, no, definitely not. I haven't felt like I'm moving in slow motion or... or struggling to get my words out at all. I'm actually pretty mindful of how I present myself, especially since I need to be sharp for the people I work with, you know? 

I think my pace is completely normal. I mean, is... is my speech sounding okay to you today? I really hope I'm communicating everything clearly for your notes. I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and being as helpful as I can.
Have you been hearing any voices that other people can’t hear?

Oh! Um... no, definitely not. Goodness, no. I haven't heard anything like that. I mean, working in mental health myself, I... I know exactly what a question like that usually points to, and I can promise you I'm not experiencing anything along those lines. My thoughts are very much my own. 

I would absolutely tell you if I was, though. I want to be completely cooperative and honest with you. But no, no voices at all. I... I hope I'm not coming across as defensive or anything? I just really want to reassure you that I'm doing okay and that my mind is clear. Am I still giving you the information you need?
How much has this been interfering with your work and daily life: has it been just a mild difficulty, or does it feel clearly marked?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it's clearly marked or anything drastic like that. I'm still showing up to work every day, and I'm really trying my best to keep everything running smoothly. I care so much about my clients, and I'd never want to let anyone down. 

I mean, I suppose... well, there have been a couple of minor things. I did miss a few grant deadlines recently, which isn't like me at all, and... and my supervisor has quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. But I think she was just trying to be helpful and lighten my load a bit, you know? It's just a mild difficulty right now, just me not functioning at my absolute usual level. 

But I'm really working on getting back on track. I don't want anyone to think I'm incapable or failing at my job. Does... does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound too bad. I just want to be honest with you so you have the right information.
